data.one_liner: Type-safe code generator for communication between Flutter and host platforms.
data.what_it_does: Generates structured, type-safe Dart and native host platform code (Kotlin, Java, Swift, Objective-C, C++, GObject) from an interface definition file. It replaces manual platform channel serialization and string-based method routing with generated message codecs and typed method interfaces. It also provides a direct native interop mode using FFI and JNI for high-performance and synchronous host calls.
use_when: Building Flutter plugins or apps with extensive custom native platform integrations.
Eliminating manual string-based MethodChannel messaging and binary buffer encoding errors.
Needing type-safe bidirectional communication (Host APIs and Flutter APIs) across iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, or Linux.
avoid_when: Exposing generated classes directly in your package's public API, as generated code changes frequently between versions.
Your project only needs trivial, one-off platform channel calls where code generation adds unnecessary complexity.
strengths: Supports multiple host targets: Android (Kotlin/Java), iOS/macOS (Swift/Obj-C), Windows (C++), and Linux (GObject).
Offers both standard platform channels and high-performance native interop (direct Dart FFI and JNI).
Generates typed data models, error handling, asynchronous wrappers, and event channels.
weaknesses: Frequent breaking changes in generated code across package updates make it unsuitable for public API exposure.
Native interop mode is complex to set up and has preview limitations regarding multi-engine routing.
data.setup_notes: Requires defining an API schema Dart file outside lib/, running the Pigeon CLI generator, and integrating generated native source files into platform-specific build configurations (Xcode, CMake, Gradle).

alternatives.name: ffi
alternatives.why_pick_it: Use when calling C or C-compatible native libraries directly without needing platform channel code generation for mobile frameworks.
